To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

reducing the share of human-edible concentrate feeds in livestock production, while increasing the share of by-products, can reduce the environmental impact of livestock production and increase food availability.

a strategy of reducing feed components that compete for land with human food production can provide sufficient food, and reduce environmental impacts of the global livestock sector, but only if animal products in human diet are reduced considerably.
a strategy of feeding livestock with less food-competing feeds can provide sufficient food and reduce the environmental impacts compared with current practice.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the impacts of a strategy that reduces the amount of feed components that compete directly with human food consumption, and we show that this strategy has considerable potential for sustainable livestock production.
the potential to reduce adverse environmental impacts of livestock production by focusing on feed components that do not compete with human food production.
the question how the livestock sector can contribute to sustainable food systems, and how it can be integrated in the global food system in a sustainable way.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the livestock sector can be a part of the solution for global food system sustainability if the share of feed components which directly compete with food production is reduced.

the livestock sector can be made more sustainable, but that this requires a combination of several strategies, and that the choice of strategies depends strongly on the specific environmental and societal goals.
all three strategies should be pursued simultaneously.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reducing the share of human-edible feed components in animal production systems can be a viable strategy to increase the sustainability of livestock production.
the livestock system could become sustainable if it is fed with non-food components and if the consumption of animal products is reduced to a level that is not much higher than the level of 1970.
, in order to achieve a sustainable food system, the share of animal protein in human diets needs to decrease and livestock production needs to become less resource intensive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a considerable room for improvement in livestock systems, which can be achieved by focusing on feed components not competing with direct human food production.
a significant reduction of food-competing feed components for livestock production could provide enough food and significantly reduce the environmental impacts of food production.
a reduction in food-competing feedstuff for livestock could provide sufficient animal protein for the world population, while reducing the environmental impacts of the food system.
